elements.text:
**Problem 1 — Diagrams drift away from the code**
Architecture diagrams live in a separate tool, so they rot the moment the code changes. Nobody trusts a six-month-old diagram.

**Problem 2 — Your diagrams are trapped in someone else's cloud**
Most whiteboard tools store your work on their servers, in their format. Leave the tool and you lose your diagrams.

**Problem 3 — No real version history**
"What did this diagram look like last release?" Most tools can't answer that — or hide it behind a paid tier.

**Problem 4 — Diagrams aren't part of code review**
You can't diff or review a diagram in a pull request the way you review code. Visual decisions happen off to the side, undocumented.

**Problem 5 — Collaboration means buying seats for everyone**
Inviting a teammate or a client to look at a board often means another paid account and another login.

**Problem 6 — AI can't touch your visual work**
LLMs are great at reasoning about systems, but they can't draw the diagram on your board — you copy-paste text and redraw by hand.

**Problem 7 — Privacy and control**
For sensitive architecture, you don't want your diagrams sitting in a third-party SaaS you don't control.
